search_queries: targeted: expat, libxml2, mxml, yxml, libroxml, ezxml, sxmlc
cells.ranking_metric: Debian popcon installations of the lead's runtime library binary package (max when two sonames are listed)
cells.selection: expat (libexpat1 297,134) and libxml2 (libxml2 binary 290,724) are the two format-aware C XML parsers with the highest Debian popcon counts; both are verified. Homebrew 365-day installs give the same order (expat 1,360,500, libxml2 564,778).
cells.uncertainty: Pilot cell: two third-party paths (expat 2.10.0 and libxml2 2.15.4) were built, matched the exact namespace-resolved summary of both valid controls under LLVM source coverage, and have native AFL++ feedback with a stable valid-control differential. They are distinct parser families. expat leads libxml2 by 6,410 installs (2.2%) on the binary-package metric, a near tie. The Debian sourcemax table would invert the order (libxml2 source 61,109) only because the libxml2 source now builds libxml2-16 and the older libxml2 binary is no longer attributed to it, so binary runtime-library counts are the primary metric; libxml2-16 (9,413) is not added because hosts may have both. Popcon counts installations, mostly pulled in as dependencies, not direct parser use. Search was the Conan Center recipe-name substring 'xml' (9 hits, 1 of them a C XML parser) plus seven targeted C names; Conan and Debian miss vendored single-file parsers. The control oracle (controls/xml/check_controls.py) uses Python's pyexpat, the same family as expat but not libxml2, so the libxml2 match is a cross-family check. The expat harness pins XML_SetHashSalt so AFL++ maps are reproducible; libxml2 needed no such change. ISO C documents no XML API. Two valid UTF-8 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, entity, encoding, XML 1.1 or rejection behaviour.

cells.uncertainty: One verified path; no padding. Search is a substring match over all Homebrew formula names and descriptions for seven queries, captured 2026-11-17; it misses header-only decoders that are not packaged there. minimp3 and dr_mp3 have no value on the primary metric, so their GitHub stars are recorded as supplemental only and are not compared with Homebrew counts. libmad is an unresolved independent family. Homebrew installs measure macOS/Linux package demand for the whole mpg123 distribution (player and library), not direct use of the decoding API. libmpg123 is the same engine counted under mp3_id3v2/c. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

cells.selection: Xerces-C++, pugixml, and TinyXML2 are verified and ranked by Debian -dev package installs: 2,676, 1,503, and 487. They are distinct parser engines. TinyXML2 leads the secondary Homebrew install-on-request metric (1,757), so the order is metric-dependent.

Both TinyXML2 and pugixml preserve qualified names but leave namespace resolution to the adapters, which is explicitly separated from library parsing. libxml++ remains unresolved and shares the libxml2 C parser family. Whole frameworks are not ranked by framework-wide installs. Two small valid UTF-8 controls cannot establish complete XML 1.0, DTD/entity, encoding or malformed-input behavior.

cells.selection: taglib (4,118) is the only C++ library among the 25 Homebrew hits with a documented local byte/stream API that parses MPEG frame headers. Its MPEG::File over a ByteVectorStream reports version, layer, sample rate, channels, bitrate and duration for both untagged Layer III controls. Higher-ranked mpg123 (12,256) and lame (6,992) are C libraries and belong to the C cell; the C++ hits mp3val, mp3check, mp3blaster, ncmdump and mp3fs are programs without a documented library API.
cells.family: TagLib MPEG frame-header and tag parser; the same TagLib 2.3.2 library as the active mp3_id3v2/cpp taglib entry. This is a separate plain-frame scope, not an independent parser family.
cells.uncertainty: One verified path; no padding. Search is a substring match over all Homebrew formula names and descriptions for six queries, captured 2026-11-17; header-only C++ decoders and vcpkg/Conan packages were not searched. Homebrew installs measure demand for the whole TagLib distribution, mostly as a tag library, not use of its MPEG property API. TagLib parses frame headers and does not decode audio; for CBR streams without Xing/VBRI its duration comes from stream size and the first frame's bitrate. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

Five Go JSON paths passed two valid structure-aware controls, source-scoped coverage and stable AFL++ feedback: json-iterator/go (18,454 Imported by), tidwall/gjson (10,420), ugorji/go/codec (10,142), goccy/go-json (4,192), and buger/jsonparser (2,171). GJSON and buger/jsonparser are path-query parsers, and their adapter traverses every value in the controls; buger/jsonparser is not claimed to validate an arbitrary complete JSON document. go-codec is multi-format: its Imported by count measures the package across several formats, not JSON-specific use. sonic (2,428) and three other numeric leads remain unverified, so the fifth path is not a definitive fifth most-used parser. Pilot cell: the three highest Imported-by XML parser leads (etree 2,098; xmlquery 627; mxj 553) were built and control-verified. All three use the Go encoding/xml Decoder tokenizer and build their own trees or maps; none is an independent tokenizer. mxj's map drops namespace URIs and prefixes, order between differently named siblings, comments, processing instructions and mixed-content runs, so only its map paths, attribute keys and trimmed text are claimed. 13 further numeric leads remain unresolved and are not selected or ranked. The first 100 hits of six queries were captured (xml dom returned 68; xml reader 28). The two small valid UTF-8 XML 1.0 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, entity declaration, non-UTF-8 encoding, XML 1.1, or attribute-value normalization behaviour.

cells.uncertainty: One verified path; no padding. Search is bounded by five pkg.go.dev queries at 100 hits each. Leads in leads.json are not verified parsers. Two valid controls do not establish complete Layer III support or independence from the mp3_id3v2 go-mp3 entry.

Pilot cell: ten JSON package/API paths are control-verified and runnable. Jackson databind and core share a tokenizer family; Gson, fastjson 1.x, org.json, fastjson2, json-simple, json-smart, Moshi, and Parsson are separate parser families. Fastjson 1.2.83 has its own DefaultJSONParser/JSONLexer; the com.alibaba:fastjson coordinate adoption metric sums both 1.x and later 2.x fastjson2 facade releases, so it is not a 1.x-only count. Its pinned-release direct-dependent count is separately recorded. Json-simple 1.1.1 is an older 2012 release with a high default-release count, so ranking uses the common deps.dev summed metric. Json-smart is verified on its RFC 4627 object/array mode, not scalar roots. Parsson implements Jakarta JSON-P with its own tokenizer over a local InputStream; the Jakarta API jar supplies interfaces. Three numeric leads remain unverified. Maven Central search is bounded to 100 hits per query (322 unique hits); deps.dev counts measure package adoption, not JSON-specific use. Two valid nested controls do not establish complete format coverage.

Six third-party XML package paths are verified and runnable: Jackson XML, Xerces2-J, Woodstox, dom4j, XMLBeans, and Aalto. Xerces2-J, Woodstox, and Aalto are independent tokenizer/parser engines. Jackson XML is a format-specific token projection over Woodstox; its ordered output omits namespace URIs, root name, comments, processing instructions, and attribute-versus-child origin. dom4j and XMLBeans build their own trees over JAXP SAXParserFactory, which selects the OpenJDK Xerces fork in the pinned runtime. XMLBeans 5.4.1 does not bundle the Piccolo parser previously suspected. Each wrapper’s own source coverage and underlying parser coverage are reported separately; AFL++ feedback is scoped to wrapper source. The standard javax.xml.parsers path is counted separately and shares the Xerces2-J family. Eight documentation leads remain unresolved, including legacy dom4j:dom4j, which is not counted beside org.dom4j:dom4j. Maven Central search is bounded to 100 hits per query (345 unique hits); deps.dev summed direct dependents measure package adoption, not XML-specific use or independent tokenizer families. Two small UTF-8 XML 1.0 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, external-entity, schema, non-UTF-8, or XML 1.1 behavior.

Maven Central Solr search ranks by relevance, the phrase queries 'mp3 decoder' and 'mpeg audio' returned 0 hits, so leads were looked up directly on deps.dev and logged in leads.json. deps.dev public coverage is incomplete and jcodec's count covers the whole codec library, not MP3 use alone. Pilot cell: five high-download package/API paths have valid nested-object and nested-array controls, package parser coverage, and AFL++ feedback; four independent parser families are represented. jsonparse (105,362,611 downloads) has no API in its README; Parser.write(Buffer) is evidenced by packaged examples and tests. The adapter requires one root and checks the parser stack and tokenizer state. JSONStream (56,299,470 downloads) is a separate stream API path over the same pinned jsonparse 1.3.1 tokenizer, not an independent engine. JSONStream.parse([]) emits one root according to packaged code and tests despite its README statement. Its private parser exposes no end-of-input completeness check: the adapter requires one emitted root, no error, and stream end, but trailing unfinished syntax after a complete root may go undetected. JSONStream own package source is covered; differential feedback on the valid controls arises only in underlying jsonparse source. @streamparser/json receives the entire Buffer and checks trailing bytes after the first root for whitespace. Other high-download leads use string-only APIs, superset grammars, or delegate to JSON.parse. Downloads cover 24 hand-picked candidates, not every search hit. Standard JSON.parse is separate. Two valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

Pilot cell: saxes 6.0.0, sax 1.6.1, fast-xml-parser 5.12.1, @xmldom/xmldom 0.9.12, and xml2js 0.6.2 are control-verified, source-covered, and have input-dependent AFL++ feedback. Comparable 30-day npm downloads rank the five package paths; counts include transitive adoption. saxes and sax share historical fork lineage but have distinct parser code. fast-xml-parser has its own scanner and validator but no namespace URI resolution, so the adapter resolves expanded names over its qualified names and xmlns attributes. @xmldom/xmldom has its own XMLReader tokenizer and DOM builder, accepts locally decoded text, and the adapter treats every warning or error as fatal. xml2js builds an ordered tree over the same pinned sax 1.6.1 tokenizer as the selected sax path; it drops comments and processing instructions, which can merge adjacent text segments. Its own package and underlying sax source coverage are recorded separately. jsdom remains an unverified route sharing the saxes family. The search is bounded to recorded queries and snapshot; two valid controls do not establish complete XML 1.0 compliance.

Search is six npm queries of 100 hits each, captured 2026-11-17; downloads were fetched for 15 hand-picked candidates, not every hit. mediabunny was found by `mp3 frame`, `mp3 duration` and `mp3 demuxer`, not the narrower queries. Its download count covers the whole media toolkit (muxing, conversion, many containers), not MP3 demuxing alone. cells.ranking_metric: PyPI Stats last_month downloads excluding known mirrors
cells.selection: mutagen (10,748,990) and tinytag (4,453,166) are the two most-downloaded candidates whose own Python source parses MPEG Layer III frame headers from a documented byte or file-object API. av, soundfile, pydub and librosa rank higher but hand frame parsing to native FFmpeg or libsndfile/libmpg123, or to an external ffmpeg process; audioread (7,283,376) ranks between the two and dispatches to native backends.
cells.shared_family: Same Mutagen package, release 1.48.1 and mutagen/mp3 module as the mp3_id3v2/python mutagen entry. This cell checks MPEGInfo on untagged streams; it is not an independent parser family. tinytag is an independent pure-Python family (its _MPEG class in tinytag/tinytag.py).
cells.uncertainty: Two verified paths; no padding. The name search is a substring filter over the PyPI Simple index (serial 43764887) captured 2026-11-17; the 'mp3' and 'mpeg' hit lists were not triaged one by one, and download numbers were fetched only for 13 named candidates, so a less obvious frame parser could be missed. Native wrappers (av, soundfile, audioread, pygame, pymediainfo, miniaudio) are unresolved, not rejected: their parsers are real but outside Python source coverage. eyed3, hachoir and pymp3 are unresolved pure-Python leads. Mutagen reads headers and checks frame syncs but does not decode audio; for CBR streams without Xing/Info/VBRI its duration is stream bytes divided by the first header's bitrate. TinyTag also only reads headers: after five equal-bitrate frames it estimates duration from stream size and mean frame length, and it does not expose MPEG version, layer or frame count. Both full-length controls run the same TinyTag lines; its feedback difference is shown with a valid three-frame prefix of the 44.1 kHz control. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

Nine verified Rust JSON parser paths selected within the first 100 hits of six crates.io queries (600 hits, 476 unique), captured 2026-11-17. Twelve documented leads remain unverified, including higher-download ijson (1,818,125) with unresolved shared-family status, so this is a bounded pilot rather than a complete top-ten ranking. Downloads are 90-day adoption proxies that include transitive pulls. gjson is a path-query parser: its parse/get calls assume valid input, so the adapter first calls its own whole-root valid function and then traverses every child through Value::each. The Rust and Go tidwall GJSON packages share design/maintainer lineage but have separate source implementations. Two small valid controls establish only their observed RFC 8259 structure; duplicate keys, huge numbers, deep nesting and non-UTF-8 are untested.

Four verified XML parser implementations selected within the first 100 hits of seven crates.io queries (642 hits, 483 unique), captured 2026-11-17. Twelve documented leads remain unverified. The xml-rs 1.0.0 package has 32,180,109 recent downloads but is a compatibility re-export of the xml package, so it is excluded as a duplicate family. Downloads include transitive pulls and are adoption proxies; ranks compare selected independent paths only. The xmlparser tokenizer does not resolve namespaces or validate tree structure; its adapter provides those observations. Two small UTF-8 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, external entity, non-UTF-8 encoding, XML 1.1, or redundant namespace redeclaration behavior. RustyXML 0.3.0 passed valid-control parsing but exact repeatable AFL++ feedback was not established; see data/rust/xml/rustyxml-feedback-audit.md.

Search covers only the first 100 hits of six queries (591 hits, 350 unique) captured 2026-11-17; the 'mp3' query alone reports 1119 matches. Recent downloads include transitive dependency pulls (Symphonia is a dependency of rodio and others) and are an adoption proxy, not evidence of direct MP3 parsing use. cells.selection: Four Packagist-ranked paths have passed valid controls: seld/jsonlint (252,371,311 downloads), laminas/laminas-json (35,102,503, forced own PHP Decoder), halaxa/json-machine (30,443,415, own stream Parser plus ext/json member decoding), and salsify/json-streaming-parser (7,715,575, own character state machine with listener events).
cells.uncertainty: Four PHP JSON third-party paths passed valid nested object controls and source-line coverage. Laminas, JSON Machine and salsify also passed a valid nested array control and stable source-line AFL feedback. Laminas is abandoned, and its own decoder runs only when explicitly enabled; its default API route delegates to ext/json. JSON Machine shares ext/json for member decoding. salsify accepts only object/array roots and silently accepts concatenated documents, so its harness rejects anything other than one complete document; the tree-building listener is harness code. Four own-parser or partial-own-parser leads remain unverified; four json_decode wrappers are excluded. The bounded search used five Packagist queries of at most 100 hits each. Package downloads measure overall/historical adoption, not JSON parsing frequency. Valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

cells.selection: sabre/xml 4.1.0 (Packagist 39,858,833), a package API over the libxml2 family: Sabre\Xml\Reader extends XMLReader and builds its own Clark-notation element tree. Both valid controls match the expat oracle on elements, attributes, depth, root and text.
cells.uncertainty: Pilot cell, one verified third-party path. The earlier zero count wrongly excluded libxml2-family wrappers; PROTOCOL.md lets a wrapper qualify as a package API with its parser family identified, so sabre/xml is counted with family libxml2 (shared with the standard XMLReader path). symfony/dom-crawler and jms/serializer stay excluded because they only navigate or map an already parsed DOM/SimpleXML tree. The other libxml2-family wrappers (veewee/xml, mtownsend/xml-to-array, saloonphp/xml-wrangler, laravie/parser, orchestra/parser, pear/xml_parser and smaller ones) were not evaluated by the cutoff and remain unresolved, as do the own-code leads prewk/xml-string-streamer and watoki/dom. sabre/xml drops xmlns declarations and text in mixed-content elements by design, so its summary omits namespace declaration counts. Its coverage image uses Ubuntu PHP 8.5.4 with libxml 2.15.2; its AFL++ overlay uses the source-built PHP 8.5.12 and libxml2 2.15.4. The search covers the first 100 hits of five Packagist queries; controls are two small UTF-8 namespace-aware documents without DOCTYPE.

This pilot covers a different module (module.audio.mp3.php frame headers, 273 lines covered on the control) of the same family, not an independent parser.

Packagist total downloads count Composer installs of the whole package (and wrappers pull getID3 transitively), not use of the MPEG frame parser. getID3 reads the first frame header, checks sync on following frames, and derives CBR duration from audio-data bytes and the header bitrate; it does not decode audio or report a frame count on these controls.
